channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Há quatro anos, Bolsonaro e Lula lançavam suas campanhas para a Presidência; lembre como foram atos
item.description: On August 16, 2022, Jair Bolsonaro and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launched their presidential campaigns in Juiz de Fora (MG) and São Bernardo do Campo (SP), respectively. Bolsonaro chose Juiz de Fora — where he was stabbed in 2018 — to deliver a conservative speech with evangelical supporters, attacking the PT and defending private property and opposition to abortion. Lula began his campaign in his political homeland, the ABC Paulista, aiming to reconnect with his working-class and union base.

item.title: Durigan diz que Brasil dá superavit aos EUA e é punido
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said Brazil is being commercially punished by the U.S. despite generating a trade surplus, citing exports of orange juice, coffee, beef, and aircraft assembled with American components. He attributed the situation to the U.S. electoral period, calling it non-structural and expecting trade flows to resume after the elections. Durigan also highlighted the opening of over 600 markets under President Lula and stressed the need for institutional, fiscal, and regulatory stability to attract investments in clean energy, critical minerals, and carbon markets.

item.title: Com pouco a oferecer ao futuro do país, Lula abre campanha olhando para o passado
item.description: Lula launched his re-election campaign by invoking nostalgic memories of his 1980s unionist past as a factory worker, contrasting it with his current status as a wealthy politician entangled in corruption schemes. While acknowledging the social achievements of his previous governments, the text emphasizes that his legacy includes a historic fiscal crisis, persistent inequality, and alliances with bourgeois parties, leading to scandals like the mensalão and petrolão. The campaign avoids addressing future challenges, instead relying on past rhetoric to deflect from Brazil’s high debt, inflation, and ongoing corruption investigations.

item.title: Ao lado de Alcolumbre, Lula visita navio-sonda da Petrobras no Amapá
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visited Petrobras' drillship in Oiapoque (AP) alongside Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, following the discovery of oil indications in block FZA-M-59 in the Amazon Mouth. Petrobras announced it had identified hydrocarbons in an exploratory well in the Foz do Amazonas sedimentary basin, with production expected to begin within seven years. The visit marks the first joint public appearance between Lula and Alcolumbre after their political rapprochement, emphasizing the economic and social potential of exploration for Amapá and Brazil.

item.title: Eleições na Bahia: o estímulo ao voto Lula-Neto
item.description: The campaign of ACM Neto, candidate for governor of Bahia, has been encouraging voters to support Lula through social media influencers, promoting the idea of a 'Lula-Neto vote' as a strategy to attract petista voters. The subscriber-only article details this tactical political alignment between seemingly opposing campaigns. It highlights the growing influence of social media and influencers in shaping voter opinion in the state.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro retornam à zona de conforto em eleição que será decidida fora dela
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro launched their campaigns by returning to their political strongholds to energize their bases, with Lula in São Bernardo do Campo and Flávio in events aligned with bolsonarismo. Both sought to reaffirm their political identities through emotional and symbolic acts, but acknowledge that the 2026 election will be won by convincing voters outside their comfort zones. Lula emphasized future-oriented proposals such as critical mineral exploration and a new public security approach, while Flávio aims to balance bolsonarist mobilization with the need to attract moderate voters.

item.title: Quaest: 73% desaprovam uso de inteligência artificial nas campanhas dos candidatos
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 73% of voters disapprove of AI use in political campaigns, with only 21% in favor. The backlash intensified after Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign used an AI-generated deepfake of Jair Bolsonaro, which the PT challenged as illegal early campaigning. The TSE has scheduled a meeting on the issue, and Quaest and Datafolha will continue releasing polls through October 3.

item.title: “Torravam a aposentadoria na Europa”, acusa Flávio sobre Lulinha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), presidential candidate, accused Lulinha — son of President Lula — of spending pension funds on expenses in Europe, based on messages exchanged with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, who is under investigation by the Federal Police for suspected influence peddling. The claim was posted on X (formerly Twitter) on Monday, the 17th. The accusation fits into the broader political conflict between opposition and government over alleged privileges and misuse of public resources.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cancela ida a Juiz de Fora por mau tempo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro canceled his scheduled visit to Juiz de Fora (MG) due to adverse weather conditions preventing takeoff from Rio de Janeiro. The location held symbolic significance as the site of his father's 2018 stabbing attack, and Bolsonaro himself had faced a knife threat two days prior. His agenda in Belo Horizonte remains confirmed, including the launch of Flávio Roscoe's Minas Gerais gubernatorial campaign.

item.title: PCB traz Edmilson Costa como candidato à Presidência
item.description: Edmilson Costa, 76, an economist and professor, is the Brazilian Communist Party (PCB) candidate for President in 2026, with Cleusa Santos as his running mate. A native of Pedreiras (MA), he has been active in politics since the 1980s, previously ran for mayor of São Paulo in 2008 and for vice president in 2010. He holds a PhD in economics from Unicamp and serves as the party’s general secretary.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula mantém vantagem de cinco pontos sobre Flávio Bolsonaro na largada
item.description: Lula holds 41% of voting intentions in the first round, five points ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (36%), according to the 10th BTG/Nexus poll. The lead remains unchanged from the previous round. In a potential runoff, Lula leads 47% to 44%, within the margin of error, while 50% of voters reject Flávio and 48% reject Lula, underscoring deep polarization.

item.title: Rede social X muda regras de algoritmo para eleição no Brasil. Entenda
item.description: Social media platform X changed its algorithm to stop recommending accounts and posts of candidates registered with Brazil's TSE during the 2026 electoral period, complying with Resolution No. 23.610/2019. Effective August 16, the change excludes such content from the 'For You' feed, though it remains available on official profiles. X implemented the 'Brazil2026ElectionFilter' to meet the requirement, stating the move aims to reduce unsolicited reach of electoral material.

item.title: O custo da promessa
item.description: The article examines the historical record of fiscal adjustment promises by Brazilian presidents, noting that only Itamar Franco and Fernando Henrique Cardoso delivered sustained primary surpluses, while Lula’s first term partially fulfilled the goal and Dilma, Temer, Bolsonaro, and the current Lula administration failed. The current primary deficit of R$ 157.2 billion over the last 12 months and projected public debt at 83% of GDP in 2026 underscore a persistent structural fiscal challenge despite repeated promises.

item.title: Flávio cancela ida a Juiz de Fora, cidade onde seu pai levou facada em 2018
item.description: Presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) canceled his scheduled visit to Juiz de Fora (MG) for this morning, the city where his father, Jair Bolsonaro, was stabbed during a campaign event in 2018. The reason for the cancellation was not specified in the released information.

item.title: Gabriel Brazão, goleiro do Santos, provoca torcida e comissão do Vasco
item.description: Santos goalkeeper Gabriel Brazão provoked Vasco da Gama’s fans and technical staff after Santos won 3-0 at São Januário in a crucial relegation battle. In a viral video, Brazão celebrated facing the Vasco bench and, when confronted by staff member Ricardo Benarroz, replied sarcastically: 'House? What house?'. Santos eased relegation pressure, while Vasco remains in danger of dropping to Série B.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula antecipou a herança dos filhos?
item.description: O Globo reported that President Lula (PT) may have anticipated the inheritance of his five children over the past four years, which could explain a 35% drop in his declared assets to the TSE. According to the report, Lula told his children he wanted to leave them well off. The story was first published by O Antagonista.

item.title: Brasil garante imunidade a observadores da OEA nas eleições
item.description: The Brazilian government has granted privileges and immunities to OEA election observers for the October 2026 elections, protecting them from arrest, judicial proceedings, and interference with their property and communications. Signed in Washington on August 13, the agreement aims to ensure the mission's independence and will remain in effect until the electoral observation concludes.

item.title: Nunes Marques reúne representantes de embaixadas, inclusive dos EUA, para defender urnas eletrônicas e tratar de IA na eleição
item.description: TSE President Nunes Marques met with embassy representatives, including from the U.S., to defend electronic voting machines and address AI use in the 2026 elections, emphasizing the machines as a 'patrimony of the Brazilian people' and outlining contingency plans against deepfakes and mass disinformation. The meeting followed a U.S. embassy request for a visit, denied by Itamaraty amid Flávio Bolsonaro’s challenges to the electoral system, and is part of broader dialogues with international Electoral Observation Missions.

item.title: Alcolumbre acompanha Lula em visita a navio-sonda da Petrobras no Oiapoque após reaproximação
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre accompanied President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on a visit to a Petrobras drilling vessel in Oiapoque (AP), following the discovery of hydrocarbons in the Morpho well in the Equatorial Margin. The meeting signals a renewed relationship after months of estrangement over the rejection of Jorge Messias’ STF nomination, leading to the advancement of key federal agendas in the Senate, including PECs on 6x1 work schedule and public security, and a bill on critical minerals and rare earths.

item.title: Quaest: 48% não acha possível interferência estrangeira nas eleições 2026, 45% acredita que sim
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 48% of Brazilians do not believe foreign interference is possible in the 2026 elections, while 45% think it is. Among those who see foreign interference as possible, 57% believe it would benefit right-wing candidates, rising to 71% among Bolsonaro supporters. The survey interviewed 2,004 voters aged 16+ between August 10–13, with a 2-point margin of error at 95% confidence.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cancela motociata em Juiz de Fora (MG) nesta segunda por 'mau tempo'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro canceled a motorcycle rally and campaign speech in Juiz de Fora (MG) citing 'bad weather', though the Federal Senate Police had executed search warrants against a suspect who posted threats against him online, including the phrase 'This time, leave it to me' with knife emojis. The city is where his father, Jair Bolsonaro, was stabbed during a 2018 campaign event. His Belo Horizonte schedule remains unchanged.

item.title: Lula e Alcolumbre têm primeiro encontro público após reaproximação em visita à operação da Petrobras na Margem Equatorial
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre will have their first public meeting after months of estrangement, visiting a Petrobras operation in the Equatorial Margin where oil and gas signals were found in the Morpho well. The rapprochement follows three private meetings in recent days, including at the residence of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes and at the Alvorada Palace. Alcolumbre, a longtime advocate for exploration in the region, celebrated the discovery as the result of years of struggle to develop Amapá and Brazil.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro alega mau tempo em MG e cancela agenda em Juiz de Fora
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL party's presidential candidate, canceled his scheduled event in Juiz de Fora (MG) due to adverse weather conditions that prevented aircraft takeoff and landing. He was set to participate in a motorcycle rally and a rally at the site where his father, Jair Bolsonaro, was stabbed in 2018. His Belo Horizonte agenda remains confirmed, where he will attend the launch of Flávio Roscoe's gubernatorial campaign in Minas Gerais.

item.title: O telefonema que deu ao brigadeiro a certeza de que o Exército não apoiaria o golpe de Bolsonaro
item.description: Brigadeiro Carlos Baptista Junior, then commander of the FAB, describes in his book how military commanders attempted to delay the clock on a potential Bolsonaro-led coup by attending meetings at the Ministry of Defense between October and December 2022. The strategy was to 'trade space for time' to avoid direct confrontation, relying on Lula's inauguration to dismantle the coup attempt. He recounts that General Freire Gomes, then Army commander, told Bolsonaro he would have to arrest him if he canceled the election, creating a heavy silence in the room.

item.title: Mau tempo faz Flávio Bolsonaro cancelar motociata e comício em cidade onde pai sofreu facada
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro canceled a motorcycle rally and rally in Juiz de Fora (MG) due to bad weather preventing landing at the local airport. The senator and presidential candidate proceeded directly to Belo Horizonte, where he has a lunch with PL leaders, interviews, and will participate in a candidate launch event.

item.title: Marília Arraes lidera disputa pelo Senado em Pernambuco
item.description: Marília Arraes (PDT) leads the Senate race in Pernambuco with 29% of voting intentions, according to a Real Time Big Data poll. Senator Humberto Costa (PT) has 20% and federal deputy Mendonça Filho (PL) 18%, placing them in a technical tie for the second seat due to the 2-point margin of error. The survey, conducted August 12–15, 2026 with 1,600 respondents, is registered with the TSE under PE-06056/2026.

item.title: Reiniciar Lula é admitir seu fracasso
item.description: The PT carried out a 'reset' of Lula in an attempt to renew his image, but this move reveals the president's failure to mobilize significant street support for nearly a decade. The initiative aims to sell hope, but in practice attests to Lula's inability to maintain a consolidated popular base since his last major mobilization, when he faced the risk of imprisonment. The article criticizes the gesture as an admission of political decline and loss of relevance.

item.title: Presidente do TSE reúne embaixadores nesta segunda para defender confiabilidade das urnas
item.description: TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques meets with ambassadors on Monday to defend the reliability of Brazil's electronic voting machines, emphasizing their security and transparency. The closed-door meeting, attended by over 100 diplomats including U.S. representatives, is part of the tribunal's strategy to counter international disinformation about the electoral system, particularly following unfounded claims linking the machines to Smartmatic and alleging CIA-backed fraud schemes. This is the second such meeting in 2026, following a June session with 25 diplomatic representatives.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro não consegue pousar e cancela agenda em Juiz de Fora
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro canceled his agenda in Juiz de Fora after his campaign stated there was no clearance for his aircraft to land at Serrinha Airport. He proceeded directly to Belo Horizonte, where he has another commitment this Monday. The visit held symbolic significance, as Juiz de Fora was the site of Jair Bolsonaro's knife attack in 2018.

item.title: “Não estou neutro”, diz Cleitinho ao declarar apoio a Flávio
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) declared he is not neutral in the 2026 presidential election and announced his explicit support for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), pledging to campaign for him in Minas Gerais. He stated he had 'lost' Flávio's platform in the state due to his delay in taking a position, during the Band debate among Minas gubernatorial candidates.

item.title: TSE abre processo contra Lula por desfile eleitoreiro na Sapucaí com dinheiro público
item.description: The Electoral Justice Corregedor, Minister Antonio Carlos Ferreira, accepted a petition from the Novo party and ordered the opening of an Electoral Judicial Investigation Action (Aije) against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, over alleged economic power abuse and improper use of media in the Acadêmicos de Niterói Carnival parade, which honored Lula using public funds. The ruling only addresses admissibility; the merits remain unexamined. The defense has five days to respond.

item.title: Prévia do PIB recua 0,6% em junho, mas avança 0,2% no trimestre
item.description: The IBC-Br, a GDP preview, fell 0.6% in June compared to May but rose 0.2% in the second quarter of 2026, the weakest result since Q3 2025. Agriculture grew 1%, while industry (-1.4%) and services (-0.5%) declined. The data signals economic slowdown, with 2026 GDP projections ranging from 1.6% (Ipea) to 2.3% (government).

item.title: Governo Trump vê censura no Brasil após X mudar algoritmo eleitoral
item.description: The Trump administration accused Brazil of censorship after X altered its algorithm for the 2026 Brazilian elections, blocking recommended posts from candidates users don’t follow in compliance with a TSE resolution. U.S. Under Secretary of State Sarah B. Rogers claimed the move constitutes Brazil-mandated censorship, despite X stating the change promotes algorithmic transparency and is not a sanction. X had previously been suspended in Brazil in August 2024 for 39 days over judicial non-compliance before being reinstated.

item.title: Pedido de voto de Michelle a Flávio reduz tensão, e campanha do presidenciável busca novo ato conjunto após crise
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro publicly asked for votes for her stepson Flávio Bolsonaro during her Senate campaign launch in Ceilândia, easing tensions following a pre-campaign rift. The gesture was welcomed by Flávio’s allies, who now aim to organize a new joint public appearance to demonstrate unity, though no such event has been confirmed yet.

item.title: Lyra e João Campos estão empatados na corrida pelo governo de PE
item.description: Governor Raquel Lyra (PSD) and former Recife mayor João Campos (PSB) are tied in the race for Pernambuco’s governorship, each with 43% voting intention in the first round and 44% in the second, according to a Real Time Big Data poll released on August 17, 2026. The survey, with a 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level, interviewed 1,600 people from August 12–15, 2026, and is registered with the TSE under PE-06056/2026. Lyra’s rejection stands at 40%, Campos’ at 35%, and 60% of voters approve of Lyra’s state government performance.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro já deu a linha de como irá combater Lula: bater na tecla de que corrupção chegou ao gabinete do presidente
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro launched his presidential campaign accusing the Lula government of corruption reaching the presidency's cabinet, citing former chief of staff Marco Aurélio Santana (Marcola) and the president's son, Lulinha, as involved in a scheme with lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger. Bolsonaro's team claims new evidence, including WhatsApp conversations, will prove that Lulinha and Marcola benefited from personal payments and gifts, such as jewelry, although Lula says he trusts his son and that he will face justice if proven guilty. Despite Luchsinger's efforts to broker deals with the government — particularly in the Ministry of Health for cannabidiol purchases — Lula's advisors state no agreements were finalized.

item.title: A reação da torcida do Vasco à presença de Flávio Bolsonaro em jogo contra o Santos de Neymar
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a 2026 presidential candidate, attended the Vasco vs. Santos match at São Januário, where he was mostly met with boos and chants from Vasco fans despite initial applause. He requested an autograph from Neymar before the game, but Vasco lost 3-0, remaining in the Brasileirão relegation zone.

item.title: Pablo Marçal pede para TSE corrigir valor de patrimônio declarado em candidatura: mais de R$ 7 bilhões
item.description: Pablo Marçal, presidential candidate for PRTB, claims his declared assets to the TSE are incorrect, stating he does not own R$ 7.4 billion as recorded. He did not provide the correct value, but in 2024 declared R$ 169.5 million when running for mayor of São Paulo. His candidacy may be denied due to eight years of ineligibility following a conviction in the municipal race.

item.title: Autoridade do governo Trump cita 'censura' do Brasil após mudança de algoritmo do X para as eleições
item.description: U.S. Under Secretary for Public Diplomacy Sarah B. Rogers criticized X’s algorithmic change in Brazil that restricts the recommendation of official candidates’ content during the 2026 elections, calling it censorship, particularly targeting right-wing politicians. The change complies with TSE Resolution No. 23.610/2019, which bars platforms from including official candidate profiles in recommendation algorithms unless through paid promotion. Her remarks come amid U.S.-Brazil tensions over internet regulation, with the Trump administration reportedly considering new sanctions against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Flávio é rejeitado por 50% e Lula por 48%, diz Nexus
item.description: The Nexus poll released on August 17, 2026, shows Senator Flávio Bolsonaro with 50% rejection and President Lula with 48% rejection among Brazilian voters. In the first round, Lula leads with 41% voting intention versus Flávio's 36%; in a potential runoff, Lula has 47% and Flávio 44%, within the 2-point margin of error. The Lula government is disapproved by 48% and approved by 47%, with 42% rating its management as 'bad' or 'terrible'.

item.title: Esposa de Haddad, Ana Estela deixa Saúde e vai para a campanha de Lula
item.description: Ana Estela Haddad, wife of former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad and USP researcher, resigned as Secretary of Information and Digital Health at the Ministry of Health to join Lula’s campaign coordination in São Paulo. Her role will focus on engaging universities, public officials, and opinion leaders, leveraging her expertise in digital health and telehealth. The resignation was published in the Official Gazette on Monday morning (August 17).

item.title: Samara Martins declara R$ 33 mil em bens ao TSE
item.description: Samara Martins, the UP party's presidential candidate, declared R$33,000 in assets to the TSE, an 880% increase from the R$3,364.55 she reported in 2022 when running for vice-president. Her running mate, Raquel Brício, reiterated she has no assets to declare, as she did in the 2020–2024 elections. The filings were made public by the TSE within the final deadline for candidate registration.

item.title: Corrida ao Senado no PR tem Deltan, Curi e Gleisi na frente; petista lidera rejeição
item.description: In Paraná, former deputy Deltan Dallagnol (Novo), state deputy Alexandre Curi (Republicanos), and federal deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT) lead voting intentions for the Federal Senate in 2026. Dallagnol is the best-positioned candidate, while Hoffmann tops the rejection index among contenders. The race is polarized between center-right and left-wing figures, with strong focus on anti-corruption and public management themes.

item.title: Minas Gerais mostra que ajuste fiscal não pode ser confundido com suspensão de pagamento da dívida
item.description: Minas Gerais obtained judicial permission to suspend interest payments on its state debt to the federal government during the administrations of Romeu Zema and Mateus Simões, redirecting those funds to other expenditures. Despite claims of fiscal adjustment, suspending payments does not constitute real fiscal adjustment, as the debt remains owed — analogous to a heavily indebted person claiming to have paid their bills while merely stopping payments, which does not equate to financial resolution.

item.title: Lula tem 60% contra 35% de Flávio em 2º turno em PE, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll released on August 17, 2026, shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) 60% to 35% in a hypothetical second-round scenario in Pernambuco. In the first-round scenario, Lula holds 58% support versus Flávio’s 24%, with other candidates polling below 5%. The Lula government enjoys 61% approval in the state, while 53% of respondents say they would not vote for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Nexus: Lula e Flávio iniciam campanha com 3 pontos de diferença no 2º turno
item.description: Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) begin the 2026 presidential election campaign for the runoff with just a three-point gap, according to the BTG/Nexus poll. Lula holds 47% of voting intentions, while Flávio has 44%, with blank and null votes remaining stable. The narrow margin signals a highly competitive race from the outset.

item.title: Lula tem 47% contra 44% de Flávio no 2º turno, diz Nexus
item.description: A Nexus poll released on August 17, 2026, shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) by 47% to 44% in a hypothetical 2026 presidential election runoff, with the two candidates technically tied within the 2-point margin of error. The survey, conducted August 14–16 among 2,003 Brazilian voters and registered with the TSE as BR-03317/2026, also found Flávio rejected by 50% of respondents and Lula by 48%, while Lula’s government approval stands at 47% and disapproval at 48%.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro mantêm empate técnico no 2º turno, com 47% a 44%
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll released on Monday (17) shows that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) remain in a technical tie in the 2026 runoff, with 47% and 44% of voting intentions, respectively. The three-point difference falls within the margin of error, indicating no statistically significant advantage for either candidate.

item.title: Lula visita navio-sonda da Petrobras na Margem Equatorial
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visits Petrobras' drilling vessel in the Equatorial Margin, following the state oil company's announcement of hydrocarbon presence in the area. Petrobras disclosed the finding on Friday, and Lula is expected to comment on the matter at Oiopoque Airport in Amapá on Monday. The visit underscores the government's focus on natural resource exploration in the Amazon region.

item.title: BTG/Nexus: Para 42%, governo Lula é ruim ou péssimo; 34% consideram ótimo ou bom e 23% regular
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows that 42% of voters rate Lula's government as bad or terrible, down from 44% in the August 10 survey — a change within the margin of error. Meanwhile, 34% consider the government good or excellent, unchanged from the previous poll, and 23% rate it as regular.
